articles.title: Keerthy Suresh's Dorothy Crosses ₹10 Crore, Tamil Cinema's 10th Hit of 2026
articles.excerpt: The Karthik Subbaraj period drama bounced back on its second weekend to cross the success threshold, turning steady word-of-mouth into a rare mid-budget box-office win.
articles.image_caption: Actress Keerthy Suresh. Her period drama Dorothy crossed Rs 10 crore at the Indian box office in its second week, becoming Tamil cinema's 10th successful venture of 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Dorothy crossed $180,000 in North America in week one with expanded week-two screenings — a festival-premiered Tamil film that diaspora audiences are keeping alive on big screens.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Arijit Singh Announces Nine-City India Tour To Mark 20 Years In Music
articles.excerpt: Playback singer Arijit Singh will tour nine Indian cities from January to May 2027, marking 20 years in music with stadium-scale shows billed as the largest live production of his career at home.
articles.image_caption: Arijit Singh performs on stage with his guitar, wearing a head covering. The singer has announced a nine-city India tour running from January to May 2027, marking 20 years in music.
articles.image_credit: Courtesy of the artist via Rolling Stone India
articles.nri_angle: India's biggest live voice is staging his biggest India run — a signal for diaspora fans that the centre of gravity of Indian music's live economy is shifting homeward.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Madhav Agasti: The Tailor Who Dressed Mogambo and Built Bollywood's Villains
articles.excerpt: In a memoir five decades in the making, master tailor Madhav Agasti reveals how a seven-day, ₹35,000 assignment for Shekhar Kapur's Mr. India produced one of cinema's most enduring villain looks.
articles.image_caption: Portrait of a grey-haired man in a pinstripe suit against a textured wall, published as the lead photograph for t2online's interview with costume designer Madhav Agasti. Agasti is the self-taught tailor who designed Mogambo's costume for Shekhar Kapur's Mr. India (1987).
articles.nri_angle: Mogambo is one of the rare Hindi-film icons whose dialogue and image have survived three generations of emigration, making Agasti's hand-stitched costume a shared piece of diaspora cultural memory.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rakul Preet Singh Denies Link to IT Searches, Demands Retractions
articles.excerpt: The actress called reports linking her to the Income Tax Department's Mumbai searches "false, malicious and speculative," saying she has paid taxes since age 20 and urging retractions.
articles.image_caption: Rakul Preet Singh in a file photo. The actress has denied any link to the Income Tax Department’s recent search operations in Mumbai, calling reports connecting her name to them false, malicious and speculative, and demanding retractions.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora audiences who read the initial claims across Gulf News and Indian outlets before any official word existed, the episode shows how unverified reports travel fast — and why the denial is now the only fact on record.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Salman Khan's Maatrubhumi Clears Key Hurdle as Revised Cut Recasts China Ties
articles.excerpt: The war drama once titled Battle of Galwan has a government no-objection certificate after months in limbo — but the version audiences will see reportedly frames India-China relations in a far softer light.
articles.image_caption: A promotional still from Maatrubhumi shows Salman Khan in uniform as the war drama's lead, flanked by soldiers. The film, earlier titled Battle of Galwan, has received an I&B Ministry no-objection certificate after the makers reworked its portrayal of China.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora's Bollywood calendar, Maatrubhumi's post-Diwali release window means the film could land in North American cinemas in November, becoming one of the biggest Hindi releases of the year in overseas markets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Yami Gautam Urges Media Not to Alter Her Photos With AI: 'Should Not Be Done'
articles.excerpt: The National Film Award winner asked outlets to use her photographs in original form, a day after Jr NTR condemned an AI-manipulated video of the 'Chuttamalle' song.
articles.image_caption: Actor Yami Gautam in a portrait photograph. She posted on X on October 4 asking the media to stop using AI to alter or enhance her photographs without consent.
articles.nri_angle: The AI-likeness debate is global — Bollywood's pushback parallels Hollywood's SAG-AFTRA-era fight over synthetic performers, and diaspora audiences consume both industries' stars.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Janhvi Kapoor Takes Indian Muslin to Paris Fashion Week Gala
articles.excerpt: At the BoF 500 Gala in Paris, the actor wore a custom Pankaj S Heritage ivory ensemble in 460-count Bengal muslin — khud-rang, woven in India — with jewellery-like embellished sleeves.
articles.image_caption: Janhvi Kapoor waves in an ivory ensemble with embellished jewellery-style tassel sleeves in Paris. She wore the Pankaj S Heritage look, styled by Rhea Kapoor, to the BoF 500 Gala during Paris Fashion Week on October 3, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian star showcasing hand-woven Indian textile on a Paris runway makes it easier for diaspora readers to wear traditional craft with pride abroad — and spotlights the weaver economy behind the glamour.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Singeetam Srinivasa Rao, Director of 'Pushpaka Vimana', Dies at 94
articles.excerpt: The genre-defying filmmaker behind Pushpaka Vimana, Aditya 369 and Mayuri died in Chennai on October 3, drawing tributes from Jr NTR, Kamal Haasan and Jagan Mohan Reddy.
articles.image_caption: Singeetam Srinivasa Rao, wearing glasses and a grey polo shirt, poses outdoors. The veteran filmmaker behind Pushpaka Vimana and Aditya 369 died in Chennai on October 3 at the age of 94.
articles.nri_angle: Rao's genre-defying films — from the dialogue-less Pushpaka Vimana to the time-travel epic Aditya 369 — remain touchstones for Indian audiences abroad and proof that Indian cinema can take creative risks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Vvaan Adds Rs 2 Crore on Second Saturday as Drishyam 3 Eats Screens
articles.excerpt: Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah Bhatia's supernatural thriller slowed sharply in its second weekend against the Ajay Devgn blockbuster, but trade watchers call its Rs 55 crore run a recovery from a 'dead on arrival' forecast.
articles.image_caption: Promotional artwork for The Vvaan shows Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah Bhatia as the lead pair. The film earned Rs 2 crore on its second Saturday, taking its India nett total to Rs 55 crore.
articles.nri_angle: The film's Chhath Puja storyline resonates with the Bihar/Jharkhand diaspora in the Gulf and US, and overseas gross of ~Rs 6 crore shows it has found that audience.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Himesh Reshammiya to Headline Bollywood Music Project's 10th Anniversary in Mumbai
articles.excerpt: The one-day festival at Jio World Garden on October 24 brings 20+ artists across two stages, with tickets from ₹1,499 on District by Zomato.
articles.image_caption: Himesh Reshammiya with the team of 'Humshakals' (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: A decade-old Mumbai festival headlined by a 2000s nostalgia icon is exactly the kind of homeland live-music pilgrimage event diaspora readers plan India trips around — and tickets are live now on District by Zomato.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Richa Chadha on 'Musafiri': Bollywood 'Needs Restructuring, So It's Not Such a Big Game of Chance'
articles.excerpt: The actor's YouTube travel series explores Mumbai's disappearing corners — and doubles as her first outing as director and writer, 18 years after her debut.
articles.image_caption: Actor Richa Chadha poses for a portrait. Her eight-episode YouTube travel series "Musafiri", exploring Mumbai, premiered on September 25.
articles.nri_angle: Chadha's insistence that Musafiri be free on YouTube — watchable "in Ireland, Pakistan or Kenya" — is a direct pitch to the global audience, including the diaspora, that shaped her career.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mandaadi Nears ₹100 Crore as Day-23 Run Keeps Soori Film on Hit Track
articles.excerpt: Soori's Tamil sports drama collected 1.38 crore on its fourth Friday to reach 96.95 crore net in India, with the 100-crore mark expected over the fourth weekend.
articles.image_caption: A still from Mandaadi showing Soori in a fishing-boat sequence. The Tamil sports drama reached 96.95 crore net in India after day 23, closing in on the 100-crore mark.
articles.nri_angle: With 17.7 crore in overseas gross, the film has travelled with the Tamil diaspora in Malaysia, Singapore and the Gulf, where mid-budget sports dramas with strong word of mouth find loyal audiences.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Drishyam 3 Records 24.58 Lakh Day-One Footfalls, Bollywood's 10th-Highest Post-COVID
articles.excerpt: Ajay Devgn's franchise finale collected 62 crore net on day one, finishing just below Tiger 3 in tickets sold while out-earning it in rupee terms.
articles.image_caption: The official poster for Drishyam: The Conclusion, featuring Ajay Devgn as Vijay Salgaonkar. The franchise finale sold an estimated 24.58 lakh tickets on day one, the 10th-highest post-COVID day-one footfalls in Bollywood.
articles.nri_angle: The Drishyam brand carries a devoted diaspora following — the originals spawned multi-language remakes and strong Gulf, North American and UK audiences, where day-one shows for the finale also drew packed houses.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New Ramayana Poster Spotlights Yash as Ravana After MrBeast's Mumbai Event
articles.excerpt: The makers released a new official poster of Yash as Ravana — in a gemstone-studded crown and royal regalia — days after a Mumbai pre-release event where MrBeast's viral 'Jai Shri Ram' moment headlined the crossover push ahead of the Diwali 2026 release.
articles.image_caption: Kannada actor Yash, who plays Ravana in Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana, at a photoshoot in Mumbai.
articles.nri_angle: Worldwide IMAX release with localized versions for international markets makes this an event theatrical release for the diaspora, and the MrBeast crossover signals a deliberate play for global audiences including Indian families abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bombay High Court bars AI misuse of Samantha Ruth Prabhu's name, image, voice
articles.excerpt: Justice Madhav Jamdar granted ad-interim relief on October 1, restraining unauthorised use of the actress's identity across 18 defendants — including Meta, Google and Amazon — and ordering takedowns of AI deepfakes and morphed content.
articles.image_caption: Samantha Ruth Prabhu poses for a portrait in a yellow top and turquoise earrings against a teal background. The Bombay High Court on October 1, 2026 granted her ad-interim protection against the unauthorised use of her name, image and voice.
articles.nri_angle: The takedown order covers the global platforms diaspora audiences use daily (Instagram, YouTube, Amazon), reminding overseas fans that resharing AI-generated celebrity content can draw enforcement action wherever it lands.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Drishyam 3 Reviews: Critics Call the Finale Gripping, Hail Ajay Devgn–Jaideep Ahlawat Face-Off
articles.excerpt: Critics largely praise the final chapter of the Drishyam franchise, with the Ajay Devgn–Jaideep Ahlawat showdown and the climax earning the strongest notices, even as some reviewers flag a slow first half and convenient plotting.
articles.image_caption: The official poster for Drishyam: The Conclusion features Ajay Devgn as Vijay Salgaonkar alongside Tabu and Jaideep Ahlawat. Critics gave the Abhishek Pathak-directed finale an average of 3.5 stars across 18 published reviews.
articles.image_credit: Poster via Wikipedia (Panorama Studios / Star Studio18)
articles.nri_angle: For the global Indian audience, this finale arriving as an original Hindi screenplay — not another remake — marks Bollywood trusting its own writers to close one of its most beloved franchises, timed as the festive season's big family outing in cinemas worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Drishyam 3: The Conclusion Opens to Rs 95.1 Crore Worldwide, Bollywood's Second-Biggest 2026 Debut
articles.excerpt: Ajay Devgn's franchise finale collected an estimated Rs 66.75 crore net in India on day one, just shy of the Rs 100-crore debut mark but the second-highest Bollywood opening of 2026.
articles.nri_angle: The Rs 15-crore overseas day-one haul shows the Indian diaspora — in the Gulf, North America, and the UK — remains the swing audience that decides the fate of big Hindi releases.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nushrratt Bharuccha Airlifted to Mumbai After Spine Fracture in Bali Accident
articles.excerpt: The Bollywood actress suffered a spinal fracture during a work-cum-holiday trip to Bali, was flown back to Mumbai by air ambulance on October 2, and is expected to undergo spine surgery in the city.
articles.image_caption: Nushrratt Bharuccha; the actress was airlifted to Mumbai after a spine fracture in a Bali accident.
articles.nri_angle: Bharuccha's films are diaspora staples, and Bali's popularity with Indian travellers makes her air-ambulance evacuation a cautionary note on medical-repatriation travel insurance for Indians and diaspora families visiting Southeast Asia.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Closes Historic India Run With Rs. 504 Crore Haul
articles.excerpt: Tom Holland's Marvel epic wrapped its nine-week theatrical run with ₹504 crore net in India, becoming the year's second-highest-grossing release and setting a new benchmark for Hollywood films in the country.
articles.image_caption: Spider-Man: Brand New Day, starring Tom Holland, finished its Indian theatrical run at roughly Rs. 504 crore net. The nine-week run made it the second-highest-grossing release of 2026 in India.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora audiences abroad can see Bollywood's global stature rising as Hollywood's biggest franchise now treats India as a must-win market alongside the US and China.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Six Indian Films Head to Busan International Film Festival 2026
articles.excerpt: From Rima Das's Not a Hero to Anuparna Roy's Venice-bound Lovers in the Blue Night, six Indian features screen at Asia's largest film festival from October 6 — with more titles in the Vision Asia and Wide Angle sections.
articles.image_caption: Stills from Birds in the Dark (left) and Birds on Ice (right), two of the Indian films selected for the 31st Busan International Film Festival. The festival runs October 6 to 15 at the Busan Cinema Center in South Korea.
articles.nri_angle: Festival selections are the early signal of what diaspora audiences will see on streaming months later — Busan screenings with English subtitles are also gathering points for Indian cinema lovers in South Korea's South Asian expatriate community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Vvaan Crosses Rs 50 Crore in Week One Despite Drishyam 3 Arriving
articles.excerpt: Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah's fantasy thriller crossed Rs 50 crore net in India in its first week, with Rs 69.07 crore worldwide — just as Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3 opened to challenge it.
articles.image_caption: Sidharth Malhotra stars in the fantasy thriller The Vvaan, which crossed Rs 50 crore net in its first week.
articles.nri_angle: The Vvaan's overseas gross of Rs 5.5 crore and its mass-circuit acceptance matter to diaspora audiences whose ticket purchases increasingly decide the fate of mid-budget Hindi originals like this Sidharth-Tamannaah fantasy thriller.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CBFC Clears Drishyam The Conclusion With Zero Cuts; 150-Minute Runtime Confirmed
articles.excerpt: The CBFC passed the Ajay Devgn thriller with a U/A 16+ certificate on September 28 — no cuts, no modifications — setting up the 150-minute finale for its October 2 release.
articles.image_caption: Ajay Devgn returns as Vijay Salgaonkar in Drishyam The Conclusion, the final instalment of the Hindi crime-thriller franchise. The CBFC cleared the 150-minute film with a U/A 16+ certificate and zero cuts ahead of its October 2 release.
articles.nri_angle: The Drishyam franchise has a strong NRI following thanks to its Malayalam roots and family-thriller formula; The Conclusion opens overseas via Panorama Studios and Zee Studios on October 2.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part 1 Is Now Titled 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend'
articles.excerpt: Sony Pictures announced the official title on September 28 with a new poster, confirming a worldwide IMAX 3D release on November 6, 2026, in Hindi and English under the tagline "Mankind's greatest story comes to life."
articles.image_caption: The official poster for "Ramayana: Rise of a Legend" shows Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama holding a bow opposite Yash's Ravana against a cosmic backdrop. Sony Pictures announced the title and a worldwide IMAX 3D release on November 6, 2026, under the tagline "Mankind's greatest story comes to life."
articles.nri_angle: The film is explicitly engineered for a global audience — English version, worldwide IMAX rollout, Sony's international distribution — putting diaspora audiences in Los Angeles, London, Toronto and Sydney at the center of its release plan.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Drishyam 3 Sells 4.05 Lakh Tickets in Advance, 7th-Biggest Pre-Sale Ever
articles.excerpt: Ajay Devgn's Drishyam: The Conclusion has sold around 4.05 lakh opening-day tickets in PVR Inox and Cinepolis, ranking 7th all-time and second in 2026, with trade forecasting a Rs. 50 crore opening on Gandhi Jayanti.
articles.image_caption: Official poster artwork for Drishyam: The Conclusion, featuring Ajay Devgn (center) and Tabu (right). The film sold around 4.05 lakh opening-day tickets across PVR Inox and Cinepolis, the 7th-biggest advance sale in Bollywood history, ahead of its October 2 release.
articles.nri_angle: The Drishyam franchise has always traveled well with the Indian diaspora, and overseas screens in North America, the UK and the Middle East open alongside the Indian release, giving diaspora audiences a record-breaking reason to catch the finale in theaters.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: MrBeast's Ramayana Appearance Puts Spotlight on His $200,000 Event Fee
articles.excerpt: The world's most-subscribed YouTuber joined Ranbir Kapoor and the 'Ramayana: Part 1' team at a Mumbai event on September 26 — the same night a new collaboration between MrBeast and producer Namit Malhotra was revealed.
articles.image_caption: YouTuber MrBeast (Jimmy Donaldson) poses in a black jacket against a promotional backdrop. The world's most-subscribed YouTuber attended a September 26 "Ramayana: Part 1" event in Mumbai alongside Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and the film's team.
articles.nri_angle: The Indian epic is being marketed to a global audience — including the diaspora — and the world's biggest YouTuber chanting 'Jai Shree Ram' shows how far Indian popular culture has travelled.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
